question: In a triangle ABC, AP the bisector of ∠A, is perpendicular to BC at point P The measures of BP and PC are x and 3y, respectively: The measures of AB and AC are 4x and (5y + 21), what is the value of (x + y)?
solution:
**Given:**

∠BAP = ∠CAP

BP = x ; PC = 3y

AB = 4x ; AC = (5y + 21)

**Concept used:**

Angle bisector bisects the third side into their two corresponding side ratio.

**Calculation: ** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f817002fa8b5122a6342275a94f44c8b66c9c9fc19878814cfcd35034047a246.png] 

⇒ BP/PC = AB/AC

⇒ x/3y = 4x/(5y + 21)

⇒ 5y + 21 = 12y

⇒ 7y = 21

⇒ y = 3

Now,

In △ APB & △ APC

AP = AP (Common)

∠P = ∠P = 90° 

∠BAP = ∠CAP

∴ △ APB ≅ △ APC (By ASA)

By C.P.C.T

x = 3y

⇒ x = 3 × 3 = 9

Now, x + y = 9 + 3 = 12

**∴ The value of (x + y) is 12.**
